title: Six questions that check understanding
subtitle: Answer these before interpreting the next performance result.
items: Why cache K/V but usually not Q? Why does KDA need state recovery?
Why are TP8 + DCP8 still eight GPUs? Why does a legacy RoPE field not prove rotation?
What BF16 traffic does direct FP8 projection remove? Why is GSM8K not an LSE test?
note: Suggested answers: Future steps use new queries, while cached K/V preserve earlier context. KDA is recurrent, so rejected speculative tokens must not contaminate future state. DCP partitions context within the tensor-parallel group rather than creating another independent eight-device dimension. The K3 checkpoint uses NoPE in MLA even though generic layout names retain a RoPE-width field. Direct FP8 cached projection avoids materializing and rereading expanded BF16 K/V and avoids the separate cached-output quantizer, while retaining higher-precision accumulation and required scaling. GSM8K measures end-to-end task outcomes; LSE tests measure attention normalization fidelity and its effect on chunk merging. Each is necessary evidence for its own claim.

title: Tensor atlas: the cached-prefill path at TP8
subtitle: Shapes shown per rank; token counts depend on the current packed call.
note: Read each dimension by role. Tq is the packed number of query tokens and Tk the packed number of cached key/value tokens in this call. Twelve is the local head count, not the request count. The 192 key/query width includes 128 projected head-specific features and 64 shared-key layout features. Value width is 128. The weight's output dimension is 12*(128+128)=3,072. Other backends may transpose LSE or use different packed layouts, so this atlas is explicitly for the documented adapter. Logical shape does not determine contiguous layout; strides, alignment, scale granularity and pointer identity remain part of the kernel contract.

title: Glossary: model concepts
subtitle: Keep the mathematical role separate from the implementation.
items: Compressed feature space / learned matrix transform
note: A model concept specifies an operation or parameterization. A kernel specifies how that operation executes on hardware. FMHA means fused multi-head attention and can accept BF16 or FP8 operands. A latent is a learned lower-dimensional representation, while quantization is a numerical representation change; the two can coexist. A gate modulates information, and different gates in KDA, MLA and MoE have different meanings. Residual mixing concerns information flow across depth. LSE is a scalar per query/head used to preserve normalization when attention is partitioned. The handbook glossary includes expanded definitions and cross-references to the equations where each term appears.

title: Glossary: execution concepts
subtitle: Name the resource or mechanism before tuning it.
items: Compute unit / GPU chiplet / 64-lane execution group
Round into compact format / restore numerical units
note: HBM capacity limits residency, while bandwidth limits how quickly large tensors move. LDS is a smaller explicitly managed memory inside the GPU execution hierarchy. CU, XCD and wavefront describe different scales of parallel execution. TP shards model calculations, DCP partitions context within a TP group and EP distributes expert ownership. NUMA and CCD concern host CPU topology and should not be confused with GPU XCDs. GEMM is an operation, MFMA an instruction family and a kernel a scheduled implementation using instructions and memory. A quantization scale may be represented as a multiplier or reciprocal depending on the API, so read the contract rather than inferring it from a variable name.
